mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in three consecutive weeks (-13.3, -13.3, -15.3, -17.9), indicating an entrenched downward momentum driven by reduced shopping and leisure activity that is likely to persist into the next four weeks absent a reversal signal elsewhere.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite the prior three-week declining trend.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapsed from +26.1 to +4.6 over two weeks as outdoor recreation becomes less viable (seasonal/weather or saturation effects); this displaced recreational demand is redirected toward indoor retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 50% week-on-week from its recent peak
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat in the two weeks following a sharp PARKS drop, showing no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently suppressed TRANSIT mobility (around -22 to -25 percent) reflects an active restriction or risk-aversion regime limiting travel to commercial districts; this constraint on transit-dependent shopping trips will keep RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remained between -21.3 and -24.6 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT remains depressed at similar or lower levels, indicating transit is not the binding constraint.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous softening in WORKPLACES (from -9.4 to -8.6 but still negative) and sustained TRANSIT suppression jointly indicate reduced commuting-linked foot traffic; the combined effect of low workplace attendance and low transit use compounds to suppress nearby retail and recreation visits more than either alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain negative across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves even when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain jointly negative, indicating no compounding interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in PARKS mobility in mid-March coincides with a seasonal transition away from early-spring outdoor novelty visits; as this seasonal outdoor spike fades, overall out-of-home leisure activity reallocates toward indoor retail and recreation venues within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS peaked at 26.1 in t-2w then fell to 4.6 by t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week following the PARKS decline, suggesting no short-term seasonal reallocation.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen to 4.0 percent above baseline, signaling increased home-bound behavior; if this trend crosses and holds above the recent range, it indicates a behavioral shift toward staying local that reduces discretionary trips to retail and recreation venues over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +4.0 percent for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises even as RESIDENTIAL stays above 4.0 percent for two weeks, showing the threshold does not predict suppressed retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: A regime of elevated precaution is indicated by simultaneously negative WORKPLACES, negative TRANSIT, and rising GROCERY_PHARM (people concentrating trips on essential errands); under this precautionary regime, discretionary RETAIL_REC visits remain structurally suppressed for the full four-week horizon because essential-trip substitution crowds out discretionary mobility.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose steadily from 8.1 to 9.6 while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stayed negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks despite continued negative WORKPLACES/TRANSIT and rising GROCERY_PHARM, falsifying the essential-trip substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Under a reopening regime, any rebound in WORKPLACES mobility above its recent trough (-10.6 at t-1w) would signal renewed commuting routines that mechanically boost adjacent retail and recreation foot traffic within two weeks, since office workers resume lunchtime and after-work shopping.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -9.0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even after WORKPLACES crosses above -9.0 for two consecutive weeks, indicating no commuting-linked retail boost.
